A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 10. $600 \text{cm}^3$ would imply a radius of only about $5 \text{cm}$, more like a tennis ball than a football.

B.explanation: Matches a sphere of radius about $10 \text{cm}$ since $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \approx 4000$ to $7000 \text{cm}^3$.

C.explanation: Too large by a factor of 10. $60\,000 \text{cm}^3$ needs a radius near $24 \text{cm}$, a diameter of about $50 \text{cm}$.

D.explanation: Far too large by a factor of 100. $600\,000 \text{cm}^3$ needs a diameter of about $1 \text{m}$, much bigger than a standard football.

hints: Picture holding a standard football - its diameter is about $20$ to $25 \text{cm}$, so its radius is about $10$ to $12 \text{cm}$.
Treat the inflated ball as a sphere with volume $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ with $r$ in $\text{cm}$ to get $V$ in $\text{cm}^3$.
Cube your radius estimate and multiply by about 4, then see which power-of-ten choice from $600 \text{cm}^3$ to $600\,000 \text{cm}^3$ it is closest to.
walkthrough: A fully inflated football is almost a sphere with diameter about $22 \text{cm}$, so use a simple estimate of diameter $\approx 20 \text{cm}$ and radius $r \approx 10 \text{cm}$.
State the geometric rule for a sphere: $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.
Using a slightly larger radius of $11$ to $12 \text{cm}$ gives $V$ about $5000$ to $7000 \text{cm}^3$, still of order a few thousand $\text{cm}^3$.
The choice $6000 \text{cm}^3$ is the only one with the correct order of magnitude. This is option B
